messages:
Marie: Quick FYI — the sampleapp failed on the key rotation test in CI, looks like env precedence flipped.
Alex: ugh, details?
Marie: Repro steps:
```
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_old
export REDWOOD_PROJECT=org:proj-a
# CI injects REDWOOD_API_KEY_ROTATED but our CLI looks at REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY first
```
Marie: Error in logs:
```
2026-03-22T17:03:12Z app ERROR auth: 401 invalid_key (expected org-scoped key)
2026-03-22T17:03:12Z app INFO fallback: using project token proj-token-xyz
```
Sam: Wait, our SDK should prefer REDWOOD_API_KEY over project-scoped keys — that's what spec says.
Alex: On which SDK? Node or Python?
Marie: Node (v2.1.0) + CLI v0.9.5. Python works.
Taylor: I can reproduce locally — the env-resolution order is wrong when both REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY and REDWOOD_API_KEY_ROTATED exist.
Alex: Looks like a regression from the last change that added per-project token support.
Luis: Quick proposal: explicit precedence order: CLI args > REDWOOD_API_KEY > REDWOOD_API_KEY_ROTATED > REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY > instance metadata. Also log which source was chosen at DEBUG level.
Marie: Agreed. Also add a warning when a rotated key is present but looks expired.
Alex: I'll open a tiny PR to fix resolution in Node SDK and add a test in sampleapp.
Alex: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/421
deploy-bot: CI queued: sampleapp-e2e (node) — build #2381
Marie: thanks — can someone add a short note to onboarding guide about env var namespaces to avoid collisions (REDWOOD_ vs REDWOOD_PROJECT_)?
Taylor: adding a line now in docs PR.
Sam: For rotation, recommend ephemeral tokens by default + refresh via metadata or a local agent.
Marie: Great — let's roll the Node fix and docs note. Follow-up: can we add a linter rule in devtools to flag multiple auth vars set?
Luis: +1, I'll mock it up.
